measurement.mode: static Vite client bundle graph — no browser, no network, no rendering
measurement.browser: not applicable. The gate never launches a browser; it reads the chunk graph the Vite build emits (dist/client/bundle-graph.json) and sums, per route, the client entry chunk, the static-import closure of the route's own chunk, and the chunks of its layout ancestors (a nested route renders its parent layouts). Browser-dependent behaviour is out of scope by design — see Issue #384 (Lighthouse measurement) and #385 (score gate).
measurement.network: not applicable. Budgeted numbers are RAW on-disk bytes of the files a browser must fetch before the route is interactive. gzip -9 figures are printed for reference only and are never budgeted, because a CDN's compression settings are not part of this measurement.
measurement.cpu: not time-based. The measurement is byte arithmetic over a build artefact, so it is deterministic on any machine and independent of runner speed. Only the wall-clock cost of `pnpm run build` that produces the artefact is runner-dependent.
measurement.source_sha: the commit the run is executed at, printed as `git rev-parse HEAD`. In CI the client build and this check run in the same job against the same SHA, so a red run always names the exact tree that was measured; locally, rebuild before rerunning if the tree changed. The gate also warns (it does not fail) when the graph's recorded client assets no longer exist under its own out_dir, which is what a stale or foreign `dist/client/bundle-graph.json` looks like.
measurement.reproduce_locally: pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check
measurement.reproduce_in_ci: the `validate` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `pnpm run validate:integration`, which runs this check immediately after `pnpm run build:production`.

headroom_policy:
Every JS cap in this file is the formula output of ONE measurement: the measured `initial_js_bytes` plus at least 0.35% headroom, rounded up to the next multiple of 5,000 bytes — `ceil(measured * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000`. There is one shared CSS cap for the same reason there is one entry chunk: the initial stylesheet is a single asset every route pulls in, so a per-route CSS cap would be 18 copies of the same number.

CURRENT MEASUREMENT (Issue #724, 2026-10-31): one `pnpm run build` of this ticket branch (base `60bf4134`) measured initial JS from 626,591 B (`/admin`) to 677,246 B (`/design-system`); the shared initial CSS measured 47,182 B, whose formula output is the 50,000 B cap. Measured per route: `/` 657,304 B, `/about` 647,824 B, `/admin` 626,591 B, `/admin/` 629,984 B, `/admin/emoji-catalog` 633,479 B, `/admin/images` 636,694 B, `/admin/invitations` 635,689 B, `/admin/invitations/accept` 634,408 B, `/admin/keys` 637,432 B, `/admin/login` 631,967 B, `/contact` 639,161 B, `/design-system` 677,246 B, `/keyboard` 662,188 B, `/portfolio/` 666,053 B, `/portfolio/$slug` 668,143 B, `/projects/dotfiles` 630,970 B, `/tools/` 631,075 B, `/tools/$slug` 634,128 B. The observed slack is +0.40% (`/admin/keys`) to +1.11% (`/about`).

WHY THE CAPS MOVED DOWN (Issue #724): the previous caps were derived from a shell that carried ~1.06 MB of server-only code. The Better Auth **server** stack (the core package, Kysely, Drizzle, the SQLite dialects, the API-key plugin) was reachable from the client bundle through four admin modules' module-level imports, and `emoji-picker-react` (335 KB) was pulled into the shared entry chunk because its `EmojiStyle` / `Theme` string enums were imported as values, which defeated the `lazy()` split that was supposed to keep the picker out of first paint. The entry chunk is now 626,488 B — down 1,063,742 B (−63%) — and the picker is a separate lazy chunk. Every cap in this file is the formula output of that measurement, so every cap moved down; the CSS cap did not move (its formula output is unchanged).

WHAT KEEPS THE SHELL SMALL NOW: a byte budget can say HOW BIG a chunk is, not WHAT is in it, so it can only react to a leak by a size delta — and the historical response to a leak was to raise the cap, seven times. `scripts/check-client-bundle-server-only.mjs` (Issue #724, `pnpm run bundle:server-only:check`, declared in `quality/client-bundle-policy.json`) closes that loop: it reads the same build graph, names the module that leaked, and fails. A leak is now a named failure to fix, not a number to renegotiate.

MEASURED BYTES come from the files Rollup emitted (`writeBundle` in `vite.config.ts` -> `scripts/_client-bundle-graph.mjs`), so a cap is compared against the exact bytes a browser downloads — including the preload marker and dependency map that Vite injects after an ordinary user plugin's `generateBundle` runs. Because the entry shell is shared, a base merge that adds a few hundred bytes to the shell re-derives several route caps at once; that is why a release merge turns this gate red until the caps are re-measured with `pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check`. It is the gate doing its job, not a flaky test. Raising a cap is not machine-checked (only an `exception` is), so a cap change is expected to carry its measurement and rationale in the PR diff.

RE-DERIVED FOR ONE ROUTE (Issue #799, 2026-11-02): only `/projects/dotfiles` moved, from 635,000 B to 640,000 B. A `pnpm run build:production` of `4426ffba` measured 635,184 B on that route — 184 B above the #724 cap — while every other route stayed inside its cap, so this is one route's cap following the formula (`ceil(635184 * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000 = 640,000`), not a re-measurement of the file. The increase is the route's own closure, not the shared shell: the breadcrumb mount (`a2612bc0`, PR #795) added 3,418 B of route-added JS (4,541 B at `e3be1fa3` -> 7,959 B, the `Breadcrumbs.styles` chunk), while the shared entry grew 737 B over the same span, of which Issue #793's SectionHeading is 301 B (`e3be1fa3` 631,029 B -> `26918979` 631,330 B). No other route's cap changed.

tool_iframe.reason: Each Tool is an independent Vite build loaded inside a sandboxed iframe from /tools/<slug>/app/, so its bytes are never part of a host route's first paint. Capping it separately keeps one heavy Tool from being hidden by the host route budget and stops a Tool from inflating the host measurement. The cap is the observed `prototype` bundle (1,502,757 B JS / 8,415 B CSS) plus headroom; the Tool's own repository owns any reduction.
